lxc_d914590175e9bfca.text: First, we meet people and see their daily life.

lxc_9e2be253b5f1cc84.text: Then we learn some history and look at regions and languages.

lxc_ea877b6113fe4688.text: Next, we visit famous places and try Spanish food.

lxc_eecda4889df6efb5.text: At the end, we go to the Seville Fair and hear about flamenco.

lxc_ee94e83aeea7d005.text: Spain is in the south-west of Europe.

lxc_00c715429ff12d85.text: Many people in Spain live in big cities.

lxc_19cacae3e318ebb0.text: Madrid is the capital and the biggest city.

lxc_fc0da6c110db3fe3.text: Barcelona is another very big city.

lxc_d6a45a7721e50691.text: Other people live on islands in the sea.

lxc_a190972a2a668acc.text: So daily life can look very different from place to place.

lxc_d21911c24fdbf98d.text: Work days can feel different too.

lxc_5905c2c155b39439.text: In the past, many shops and businesses closed in the middle of the day.

lxc_50d330fdcc765938.text: They often closed for two or three hours.

lxc_907ea0d31a5d9950.text: This gave people time for a long lunch at home.

lxc_63d138b279d458a1.text: Family and friends are an important part of the day.

lxc_c2a4304c57c913d3.text: A long time ago, Muslim rulers governed a big part of Spain.

lxc_a0d45217f1b7c144.text: The city of Granada was the last Muslim kingdom.

lxc_5d923d5e63cec485.text: In 1492, it was taken by a Christian queen and king.

lxc_858e4680f8c4b3ef.text: The Alhambra in Granada is from the time of Al-Andalus.

lxc_eb0ceb0c68f8a237.text: It is an old palace and a strong building that protected the city.

lxc_21e390744af2f3bb.text: People choose their government by voting.

lxc_c84e9a2ad5f182fb.text: The country also has a king.

lxc_5a18e5621e8c463d.text: Spain is part of the European Union.

lxc_ceeda178684538a9.text: Spain has 17 regions with their own governments.

lxc_dd0d7cc262fcfaa3.text: Each region makes some of its own decisions.

lxc_653ddd6b7a255296.text: It is the language for the whole country.

lxc_49e5faa6170a0a15.text: But some regions have a second official language.

lxc_461020859477c132.text: People speak Galician in the north-west.

lxc_50f56a0333c490c7.text: People speak Basque in the north.

lxc_16231b3f4b5d52ba.text: Basque is very different from Spanish.

lxc_4ea31c7c3dbd3499.text: It is not related to most other languages in Europe.

lxc_81bafbe4fc68129a.text: Let’s connect three cities with three famous places.

lxc_a908d34b0e580963.text: In Barcelona, the Sagrada Familia is a Catholic church designed by Antoni Gaudi.

lxc_0fdf8a3c912ddcf5.text: It is the tallest church in the world, and parts of it are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

lxc_5e39c126357e853a.text: In Granada, Andalusia, the Alhambra brings us back to Al-Andalus.

lxc_ecef70bc4532b0d8.text: This old palace and fortress is a famous example of Islamic building design.

lxc_cf86a720fbc12398.text: In central Madrid, the Museo del Prado is Spain’s main national art museum.

lxc_1ffe59f7d9d08b0a.text: It opened in 1819 and has many paintings by Francisco Goya and Diego Velazquez.

lxc_eeec72ae2b39421e.text: These places offer different ways to explore Spain: through a church, a palace, or art.

lxc_63658a2d80bf7fcf.text: Lunch is usually Spain’s large main meal, starting around 2:00 to 2:30 in the afternoon.

lxc_db728e5a10bf2f8c.text: A small snack, called merienda, may come around 6:00.

lxc_56f48cb3bfb35dc3.text: After a meal, people may stay at the table to relax and talk.

lxc_0f6bab6ac2d03574.text: This time together is called sobremesa.

lxc_0de0419d66806a03.text: Paella is a Valencian rice dish from the east coast, cooked in a wide, flat pan.

lxc_7cf761619bc70acb.text: Gazpacho is an Andalusian cold vegetable soup, often made with tomato and eaten in summer.

lxc_a4e78a16233e0e02.text: Tortilla is a thick omelette with eggs and potatoes, often with onion.

lxc_2d936beac6b5d3cf.text: Tapas are small snacks that can be hot or cold.

lxc_678f7017e3e67e9d.text: Several tapas together can make a full meal.

lxc_5e97394916d4144c.text: The Seville Fair, also called Feria de Abril, is an Andalusian fair in Seville.

lxc_267dbba0d60dcf6f.text: It usually begins two weeks after Holy Week, the week before Easter.

lxc_1bc2725962e48158.text: The fair has rows of decorated tents called casetas.

lxc_fc2cb1011d647405.text: These belong to families, groups of friends, clubs, and other groups.

lxc_e15705533df60222.text: From about nine at night until early morning, people dance sevillanas, a folk dance danced in pairs.

lxc_e8a10d1bbdbbc058.text: Southern Spain is also the home of flamenco.

lxc_4f7f73629a1d7798.text: Flamenco is an Andalusian art of music, song, and dance.

lxc_2a22d52cb4ae47e1.text: The Romani people of Andalusia helped create it.

lxc_1385842735b65777.text: Like Valencian paella, flamenco has a local home, even though people know it far beyond that region.
